# `silk/schema/msgpack`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read and write `Schema` types as MessagePack.

## When to use
Call [`SchemaMsgpack.decode`](#SchemaMsgpack.impl.decode) to read a value of a `silk.schema.schema.Schema` type from
MessagePack bytes, [`SchemaMsgpack.decodeAll`](#SchemaMsgpack.impl.decodeAll) to report every problem in the bytes at once, and
[`SchemaMsgpack.encode`](#SchemaMsgpack.impl.encode) to write a value to the ambient `Writer`. Use MessagePack instead of
`silk.schema.json.SchemaJson` when the reader is a program and size or binary data matters. Use
`silk.msgpack.value.Msgpack` for MessagePack whose shape is not known in advance.

## Details
A struct is a map with one text key per field, in declaration order; a union follows the same
tag rules as in JSON. An `Option` that is `None` is `nil`, and a `None` field is left out. A
`silk.collections.bytes.Bytes` field is MessagePack binary data, not Base64 text. Integers are
written in the shortest format and read from any width, and a `float 32` is read as `f64`.

Decoding streams over the bytes with `silk.msgpack.scanner.MsgpackScanner` and builds the value
directly, with no tree in between. Each map is scanned once into an index of its entries, so
entries may come in any order, and entries the type does not name are skipped, or reported when
its spec is `Spec.strict`. Every problem carries the span of the bytes it is about.

## Gotchas
A map with a key that is not text cannot be read as a struct. An extension value, such as a
timestamp (type -1), has no schema type and is reported as `IssueReason.InvalidType` where a
field reads it; it is skipped where no field does. Nesting is limited to 64 levels.

`silk.schema.report.SchemaReport` shows problems as lines and columns of text, which MessagePack
does not have. Show a problem by its `path` and by the byte offsets of its issue's `span`.

## Examples
### Write a struct and read it back
```silk
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.writer { Writer, WriterError }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.issue { SchemaError }
import silk.schema.msgpack { SchemaMsgpack }
import silk.schema.schema { Schema }

struct Capture {
  bytes: [u8; 64],
  length: usize,
}

impl Writer for Capture {
  effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Self, value: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer {
    if self.length + value.length > 64 { fail Writer.failure() }
    Slice.copyInto<u8>(&mut self.bytes, self.length, value)
    self.length = self.length + value.length
    return ()
  }

  effect fn flush(self: &mut Self) -> () ! WriterError ? &mut Writer { return () }
}

struct Frame {
  pub id: u32,
  pub payload: Bytes,
}

impl Schema for Frame {}

effect fn check() -> i32 ! SchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let frame = Frame { id: 7, payload: run Bytes.copy(b"\xff\x00") }
  let mut capture = Capture { bytes: [0; 64], length: 0 }
  run SchemaMsgpack.encode<Frame>(&frame) |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut capture)
  let written = Slice.view<u8>(&capture.bytes, 0, capture.length)
  // {"id": 7, "payload": bin(ff 00)}
  if written != b"\x82\xa2id\x07\xa7payload\xc4\x02\xff\x00" {
    return 1
  }
  let again = run SchemaMsgpack.decode<Frame>(written)
  if again.id != 7 || again.payload.asSlice() != b"\xff\x00" {
    return 2
  }
  return 0
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! SchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run check() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

<a id="SchemaMsgpack.impl.decode"></a>

### Associated function `decode`

```silk
pub effect fn decode<T: Schema>(bytes: &[u8]) -> T
    ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads one value of type `T` from the MessagePack `bytes`, stopping at the first problem.

#### Details

The whole input must be exactly one MessagePack value. A struct is read from a map with text
keys, in any order; integers are read from any width, and `Bytes` from binary data.

#### Errors

- `SchemaError` if the bytes are not valid MessagePack, hold more than one value, or do not
  hold a `T`. Its `path` names the part that failed, and its issue has the span of the bytes
  it is about, as byte offsets into `bytes`.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the value.

<a id="SchemaMsgpack.impl.decodeAll"></a>

### Associated function `decodeAll`

```silk
pub effect fn decodeAll<T: Schema>(bytes: &[u8]) -> T
    ! SchemaErrors | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads one value of type `T` from the MessagePack `bytes`, reporting every problem.

#### Details

A field, element or variant that fails is recorded and skipped, and reading goes on with the
next one, so one call lists every problem, in input order: a missing key, a wrong type, a
number out of range and a failed rule alike. Bytes that are not one valid MessagePack value
are the one problem reported. At most `MAX_PROBLEMS` (64) are listed.

#### Errors

- `SchemaErrors` with every problem found.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the value.

<a id="SchemaMsgpack.impl.encode"></a>

### Associated function `encode`

```silk
pub effect fn encode<T: Schema>(value: &T) -> ()
    ! SchemaError | WriterError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Writer | &mut Allocator
```

Writes `value` as MessagePack to the ambient `Writer`, without flushing it.

#### Details

A struct is written as a map with one text key per field, in declaration order, without its
`None` fields. Every value takes the shortest format that holds it, and a float is always a
`float 64`. Nothing is buffered: each value goes to the `Writer` as it is reached.

#### Errors

- `SchemaError` if MessagePack cannot hold the value: text, bytes or a list longer than
  4294967295, or a value nested more than 64 levels deep. Its path is empty.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if a codec needs memory that the `Allocator` cannot supply.

## `MsgpackSchemaReader`

```silk
pub struct MsgpackSchemaReader<'input>
```

A `SchemaReader` over MessagePack bytes.

### When to use

[`SchemaMsgpack.decode`](#SchemaMsgpack.impl.decode) and [`SchemaMsgpack.decodeAll`](#SchemaMsgpack.impl.decodeAll) use it. Use it directly with
`silk.schema.schema.Schemas.read` to read a value that more bytes follow, which
`SchemaMsgpack.decode` refuses.


<a id="MsgpackSchemaReader.impl.collectingAll"></a>

### Associated function `collectingAll`

```silk
pub fn collectingAll(input: &'input [u8]) -> MsgpackSchemaReader<'input>
```

Returns a reader at the start of `input` that records every problem instead of stopping at
the first. Read them with [`MsgpackSchemaReader.intoErrors`](#MsgpackSchemaReader.impl.intoErrors).

#### Gotchas

A collecting read goes on after a failed part by reading past it, so `input` must be valid
MessagePack; `SchemaMsgpack.decodeAll` checks that first.

<a id="MsgpackSchemaWriter"></a>

## `MsgpackSchemaWriter`

```silk
pub struct MsgpackSchemaWriter
```

A `SchemaWriter` that writes MessagePack to the ambient `Writer`.

### When to use

[`SchemaMsgpack.encode`](#SchemaMsgpack.impl.encode) uses it. Use it directly to write a value inside MessagePack that the
program writes itself with `silk.msgpack.output.MsgpackOutput`.

### Details

It holds no bytes: every call writes straight to the `Writer`. An array or map header carries
the count the schema gives `beginList` and `beginObject`.
